subtopic: SQL, NoSQL and OS Command Injection Mechanics
question_text: [Web Application Security & OWASP Top 10 - Q56] Why does using parameter binding / prepared statements completely neutralize SQL injection vulnerabilities, regardless of special characters in user input?

options.text: It encrypts the entire database table
It separates the SQL statement syntax from user-supplied data, ensuring the query structure is pre-compiled by the database engine and user values are treated strictly as literals
It strips out all quotes and semicolons via regular expressions
It converts SQL queries into REST requests

answer_explanation: Prepared statements compile the query execution plan ahead of time. User parameters are passed across the wire as typed data values, so malicious characters cannot alter query structure.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: B. Rationale: Prepared statements compile the query execution plan ahead of time. User parameters are passed across the wire as typed data values, so malicious characters cannot alter query structure.
